zones._how: Photo 032 (= the owner's 0387927a, mean pixel difference 1.2 of 255) was taken from the crane parked at the NW end. A level-camera perspective fit of the nine visible columns of the left row (6 m pitch) gives rms 3.0 px, vanishing point u 624, horizon v 262 (from the runway girders), f*h 3821 px*m from two column bases, camera 6.88 m up (VGGT: 7.33), 1.7 m left of the nave axis, 3.8 m in front of the entry grid line (first visible column 14.2 m ahead = grid line s 18; VGGT puts the end wall 1-4 m behind the camera). Each marked pixel is put on the floor: D = f*h/(v - 262), lateral = (u - 624)*h/(v - 262). Cross-check: the ground photos 018-025, taken beside the press, sit 39-46 m from the crane camera in the VGGT cloud (the fit puts the press base 47 m out). Bay count in photo 032: the dance floor spans bays 1-5 from the crane, the stage front is at grid line 5 (s 30), the press stands at grid line 9 (s ~51-54), beside the expansion joint (paired columns, photo 021 taken there).

dimsSource: photographs: VGGT (Wang et al., CVPR 2025), weights facebook/VGGT-1B @ 860abec7 (CC BY-NC 4.0); photographs (perspective fit on photo 032) and the owner's marks; photographs: photo 007 (iPhone 14 Pro Max 3x tele, EXIF intrinsics) measured with scripts/place/crane_height.py on the picks in moxir-crane-picks-2026-09-29.json; photographs: 12 FUJIFILM X-T5 frames the owner sent 2026-09-29 (shot 2026-09-26 15:45-16:23 +04, no GPS; photos-2026-09-29.json beside them) + photo 007; the photos stay private; unstated

notes: Roof: a flat steel double-layer space frame (square-on-square offset grid of pyramids, star gusset nodes, corrugated deck on the top chords), photos 017, 020, 021, 023, 024, 034, 035. Bottom chord 11.0 m, top chord 13.5 m. The 'Kislovodsk' (TsNIISK) 3 x 3 m block at 2.12 m depth is a likely family — a GUESS to verify.

Lanterns: raised flat-top box lanterns 12 m wide, ~3.5 m above the deck, over spans 2 and 3 only, each line split in two ~38.5 m segments with a ~14.5 m gap at the expansion joint (Esri Wayback 37890, Maxar WV-3 2020-10-30). The satellite put the gap centre at v = -2 m from the roof centre; the roof edge and the 108 m grid disagree by 1.5 m, so the joint is taken on the grid centre line (paired columns, Soviet practice: each 500 mm off the line) and the segments are centred on it: setback 8.25 m from the end grid lines (satellite 7-8.5).

Columns: precast concrete, a solid lower shaft; at crane level the head flares SYMMETRICALLY across the hall with 45-deg chamfers (Y / goblet), one steel crane girder on each side, a centred upper column to the space frame. Not flared along the row (photo 038).
Crane runway: grey steel plate girders with web stiffeners (photo 004 right), two per inner row, a handrail along the nave-side girder.

Walls: no nave wall, no clerestory, no aisles — the four spans share one flat roof. Outer long walls only at the building edge (concrete panels, 3 ribbon window bands). Low block walls ~3 m in some bays.

Heights and the span/pitch ratio: carried over from moxir-hall-dims-2026-09-27.json (VGGT + perspective); the camera height fitted on photo 032 on 2026-09-28 (6.9 m, see the features file) agrees with VGGT's 7.3 m within 6%.

2026-09-28 hall fix (owner: 'so fix all make it right right'): the space frame is BIG — 6 x 6 m square pyramids 2.5 m deep (the chord planes 11.0/13.5 m, VGGT), star gusset nodes at every bottom node, heavy chords; the lantern keeps its own 3 m frame. v2 drew a thin 3 m lattice everywhere (wrong: the photos' module is the column pitch).

2026-09-29: crane rail 7.6 (disputed 6.6-8.4) -> 8.1 m measured; the bridge underside was DRAWN at rail + 0.55 = 8.15 m, it is measured at 7.95 m (0.2 m lower than drawn). Column heads follow the rail (head top = rail - 0.14 - 0.9 = 7.06 m, was 6.56).
What is still owed: a tape or laser distance to the crane's underside on site (one number settles it), and the entry-end crane's own underside and hook height.
